nodes.label: Medicine for Students Under Mental Stress
nodes.content: Meditation and yoga is a medicine for students who are under mental stress.

nodes.label: Panchkosh Sanjeevan Vidya
nodes.content: The revitalization-of-the-five-koshas technique used in TMT's meditation pillar: a yogic-philosophy practice that awakens the inner life-force through wisdom, by working through the five koshas (sheaths) that layer the human being — Annamaya, Pranamaya, Manomaya, Vijnanamaya and Anandamaya kosha.

nodes.label: Refining the Panch Koshas for Personality Development
nodes.content: The Panch Koshas are the five layers of our body; they need refinement for the personality development of individuals and of the community.

nodes.label: Five Daily Practices to Get Closer to Nature
nodes.content: Five things to do daily so as to get closer to nature: Jap, Tap, Yog, Yagna, and self-study and revision.

nodes.label: Jap
nodes.content: One of the five daily practices to get closer to nature.

nodes.label: Tap
nodes.content: One of the five daily practices to get closer to nature.

nodes.label: Yagna
nodes.content: One of the five daily practices to get closer to nature.

nodes.label: Mantra Yoga
nodes.content: Mantra Yoga helps students achieve easy rhythm (Sulabh Lay) and sound meditation (Nad Yoga), which in turn develop stable, rhythmic breathing and a composed mind. Through Lay and Nad, students can enhance their intellect sharpness, mental peace and blissful state.

nodes.label: Sulabh Lay (Easy Rhythm)
nodes.content: Easy rhythm achieved through Mantra Yoga; together with Nad Yoga, it develops stable, rhythmic breathing and a composed mind.

nodes.label: Nad Yoga (Sound Meditation)
nodes.content: Sound meditation achieved through Mantra Yoga; together with Sulabh Lay, it develops stable, rhythmic breathing and a composed mind.

nodes.label: Annamaya Kosha
nodes.content: The physical/food sheath — the physical body itself, made by the food we eat; the outermost of the five koshas. It is purified by pure/Sattvic food.

nodes.label: Sattvic Food
nodes.content: Pure/Sattvic food purifies the Annamaya Kosha. It also enhances sattva guna, which in turn enhances the intellect.

nodes.label: Pranamaya Kosha
nodes.content: The vital/energy sheath — vital air and energy that resides inside our body, within the Annamaya Kosha. This kosha gets purified through the Panch Pranas, namely Prana, Apana, Vyana, Samana and Udana, and through Pranayama and the sound practice Swaropasana.

nodes.label: Pranayama
nodes.content: Pranayama purifies and controls breathing. Purified and controlled breathing regulates and stabilizes a restless mind and intellect.

nodes.label: Swaropasana
nodes.content: Prolonged chanting of Om is an effective sound therapy; practicing Om is the sound practice Swaropasana, which purifies the Pranamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Prana
nodes.content: One of the Panch Pranas (five vital airs) that purify the Pranamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Apana
nodes.content: One of the Panch Pranas (five vital airs) that purify the Pranamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Vyana
nodes.content: One of the Panch Pranas (five vital airs) that purify the Pranamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Samana
nodes.content: One of the Panch Pranas (five vital airs) that purify the Pranamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Udana
nodes.content: One of the Panch Pranas (five vital airs) that purify the Pranamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Manomaya Kosha
nodes.content: The mental sheath — the layer of mind, thoughts and emotions. It gets purified through chanting, meditation, contemplation and reflection, and specifically through chanting of the Gayatri Mantra. Through mind purification, one attains intellect purification, which in turn makes the student focused and strong-willed.

nodes.label: Vijnanamaya Kosha
nodes.content: The wisdom/intellect sheath — the layer of discernment and higher knowing that guides right action. It gets purified through intellect, logical reasoning, curiosity and intellectual thinking, and through Dhyana Mudra. A pure Vijnanamaya Kosha enhances consciousness and discriminatory intelligence.

nodes.label: Dhyana Mudra
nodes.content: The meditation hand-gesture practice that purifies the Vijnanamaya Kosha; a pure Vijnanamaya Kosha enhances consciousness and discriminatory intelligence. Dhyana Mudra also helps create a balance between gastric force and the life-giving prana.

nodes.label: Anandamaya Kosha
nodes.content: The bliss sheath — the innermost layer, experienced as pure joy/bliss, where the inner life-force is fully awakened. The Upanishads describe it as the kosha that follows the first four; identifying/experiencing it is the highest development of an individual's personality and the most refined state of being. In healthy students, it indicates an enthusiastic and blissful state of mind. It is purified through self-study.

nodes.label: Self-Study
nodes.content: Through self-study, one can purify the Anandamaya Kosha. Self-study enhances mental strength and virtuous nature, and positively influences one's stream of thoughts.

nodes.label: TMT
nodes.content: TMT stands for 13 Minute Therapy — the meditation technique taught in Tripadi.

nodes.label: Atharvaveda — Shaunaka Samhita
nodes.content: The Shaunaka Samhita of the Atharvaveda elaborately discusses karmaja vyadhi (disease arising from one's own karma) and gives a detailed, precise account of Sanjeevani Vidya and Devi Chikitsa (divine healing) as its treatment.

nodes.label: Karmaja Vyadhi
nodes.content: Disease/affliction described in the Atharvaveda's Shaunaka Samhita as arising from one's own past karma.

nodes.label: Devi Chikitsa (Divine Healing)
nodes.content: The divine-healing treatment the ancient rishis prescribed for karmaja vyadhi: mantra, tantra, yoga, yajna, tapa, herbal remedies and water-based treatments are all referred to as divine treatments; Panchakarma is cited as one such example.

nodes.label: Panchakarma
nodes.content: One example of the divine treatments (Devi Chikitsa) referred to by the ancient rishis.

nodes.label: Mantra
nodes.content: That by repetition of which one can influence the mind.

nodes.label: Yoga
nodes.content: Stilling or regulating the fluctuations or modifications of the mind.

nodes.label: Mind's Hold Over the Senses
nodes.content: The mind influences our senses, pulling them toward outward worldly objects.

nodes.label: Sanjeevan Vidya
nodes.content: The knowledge of Sanjeevan Vidya, part of Upanishad and Vedanta literature, encompasses Pranopchar, Panchkosh and Gayatri Tantra.

nodes.label: Pranopchar
nodes.content: One of the components of Sanjeevan Vidya, alongside Panchkosh and Gayatri Tantra.

nodes.label: Gayatri Tantra
nodes.content: One of the components of Sanjeevan Vidya, alongside Pranopchar and Panchkosh.

nodes.label: Breath–Mind Link
nodes.content: When breathing is distracted or unstable, the mind also gets distracted.

nodes.label: Definition of Perfect Health (Swasthya)
nodes.content: One is in perfect health when Vata, Pitta and Kapha, the digestive system, bones and all other body tissues are in perfect condition, and one is satisfied or content, with the senses turned inward instead of chasing worldly objects.

nodes.label: Vata, Pitta, Kapha (Tridosha)
nodes.content: The three bodily humors — Vata, Pitta and Kapha — whose perfect condition, along with the digestive system, bones and other tissues, marks physical health.

nodes.label: Karma Yoga Without Attachment
nodes.content: One whose mind has control over their senses is considered healthy; one who can control their senses through their mind and practices karma yoga without any attachments is considered to be healthy.

nodes.label: Impure Mind Aggravates Disease
nodes.content: An impure mind aggravates chronic mental health issues.

nodes.label: Meditating on Pure Consciousness Removes Disease
nodes.content: By meditating upon the pure consciousness that resides in us all, diseases, defects and disorders are removed.

nodes.label: The Yogi's Supreme Happiness
nodes.content: When the mind is focused away from material activities through the practice of yoga, one can see this self with a pure mind and rejoice in inner bliss. The yogi with a peaceful mind, free from impurities, attains supreme happiness.

nodes.label: Taittiriya Upanishad
nodes.content: The Taittiriya Upanishad gives detailed account of the Panch Koshas that encapsulate a being's inner, pure consciousness.

nodes.label: Atman / Brahman Within the Koshas
nodes.content: The Atman — pure consciousness, one with Brahman — resides inside the five koshas. One must detach from each kosha in turn to identify one's true self.

nodes.label: Gayatri Upasana
nodes.content: Goddess Gayatri is described as five-headed, signifying the Panchkoshas. Through the specialized method of Gayatri Upasana, one can achieve purification, healing and revitalization of the Panchkoshas — one of the most important aspects of spiritual development.

nodes.label: Gayatri Mantra
nodes.content: The mantra which, when chanted with devotion, can influence and hence regulate the senses.

nodes.label: Five Elements of the Body
nodes.content: Our body is a composition of five elements of nature — Earth, Water, Air, Fire and Space. This is agreed upon by both Western and Ayurvedic systems.

nodes.label: Earth
nodes.content: Muscles, bones, skin and other physical elements of the body.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.content: Blood, water and other fluids of the body.

nodes.label: Air
nodes.content: The respiratory system, muscular movement, and the tendency to expand and contract.

nodes.label: Fire
nodes.content: Body heat, and the biochemical and bioelectric energy generated from different enzymes and the digestive system.

nodes.label: Space
nodes.content: The space existing at every level within the body's systems, from the molecular to the muscular.

nodes.label: Koshas as Layers of Consciousness
nodes.content: According to Vedic science and philosophy, our body is a combination of five layers of consciousness — Annamaya, Pranamaya, Manomaya, Vijnanamaya and Anandamaya Kosha — which are covered and overlapped around the main energy centres (Shakti Kendras) in our body.

nodes.label: Shakti Kendras
nodes.content: The main energy centres in our body, around which the five koshas are covered and overlapped.

nodes.label: What Each Kosha Feeds On
nodes.content: Each kosha feeds upon different elements of human nature, society and the environment around us. Thus any good or bad influence, or pollution of any kind, affects that layer of the body and the person themselves.

nodes.label: Health and the Four Aims of Life
nodes.content: Only a healthy and fit person can walk the path of Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha.

nodes.label: Refinement as the First Requirement of Every Path
nodes.content: Anyone who aspires to progress in bhakti (devotion), gyan (universal knowledge), karma yoga, sannyasa (renunciation) or even science, under the guidance of their guru and following any kind of upasana, must first get all five koshas refined, purified and stabilized. The first step of this process is the refinement and rejuvenation of the Annamaya Kosha.

nodes.label: Annamaya Kosha and Wellbeing
nodes.content: The Annamaya Kosha is the physical body, nourished, in a good or bad way, by the food we eat, the liquids we drink, the way we live and move around, and mostly by the actions and physical work we do. Even a small problem or imbalance in the digestive system may result in acidity, constipation or another illness, with visible effects on a person's overall health, mood and behaviour, seen as dullness and discomfort. The physical body, its systems and their balance are tightly coupled with a person's health and behaviour.

nodes.label: Mantra, Mudra, Swar, Naad and Laya
nodes.content: To address the relationship between a person and their physical body, the practice is based on five elements: Mantra, Mudra, Swar, Naad and Laya. Together they form an Ayurveda-based Panchakarma treatment for psychological and physical wellbeing.

nodes.label: Mantra (practice)
nodes.content: Recitation of any mantra, during which one stabilizes the breathing and performs dhyan (meditation and concentration).

nodes.label: Mudra (Hand Gesture)
nodes.content: During the mantra meditation one can hold Shankh Mudra or Apanvayu Mudra. A mudra holds an essence that activates and stabilizes the effect of the mantra recitation.

nodes.label: Swar
nodes.content: Different forms of pranayama.

nodes.label: Naad
nodes.content: Practising the different forms of Omkar (Om) recitation.

nodes.label: Laya
nodes.content: In the state of concentration or yog nidra (yogic sleep), the process of trying to relax and stabilize the mind and body.

nodes.label: Pranamaya Kosha and Wellbeing
nodes.content: Problems of the Pranamaya Kosha such as fatigue, anxiety, acidity and constipation can be addressed by managing the micro-environment we live in, along with some diet management. The side effects of noise pollution and depression can be addressed by musical healing therapy, and prayer healing and pranic healing (pranayama) can help cure many problems.

nodes.label: Vastu Dosh Chikitsa
nodes.content: Micro-environmental system management: structural or internal modification of the place we live in and its surroundings, along with some diet management. It addresses problems like fatigue, anxiety, acidity and constipation.

nodes.label: Musical Healing Therapy
nodes.content: Healing through music, which addresses the side effects of noise pollution and depression.

nodes.label: Prayer Healing
nodes.content: Healing through prayer, which can help cure many problems.

nodes.label: Pranic Healing
nodes.content: Healing through pranayama and prana, which can help cure many problems.
